In the remaining range the singleton clade is always hit. For the unique doubleton let X be its sample count, p_i=P(X=i). Conditioning on X=2 gives E[P_m|X=2]-E[P_m]=Hp_0-2ε(1-m/N); multiplying by -p_2 gives the covariance, since K_m=m-1_{X=2}. The hypergeometric p_0 and p_2 give the displayed formula, strict cutoff, common length ratio and N=5 witness -3/200. Binary refinement with positive, sufficiently short internal edges works by linearity/continuity and finitely many inequalities. Inspected the frozen verifier without executing it. Independently enumerated combinations(range(N),m) for N=5,6,8, every interior m and ε=1/32,1/8,3/4 at H=1: map labels 0 and 1 to the doubleton tip and each other label to its own tip, union the detected root paths, and compare exact rational E[KP]-E[K]E[P] with the formula. The sums agreed; this is only a finite cross-check.

value.rationale: Richness and rooted diversity are natural joint statistics on the same rarefied set. The theorem identifies every protected depth, including the near-census depth, and uses a single abundance profile and tree to separate all other depths simultaneously. The sharp onset at N=5 and the positive-edge phase boundary give genuine constraints on when fixed-depth co-fluctuation can reverse; they are not claims about across-community correlations or a most-negative possible covariance.
